name: Vidal Security AI
author: jmvidalg

sections.description:
Most security plugins speak in logs and codes. Vidal Security AI speaks like a person: it scans your site, gives you a clear 0–100 score, explains every problem in one plain sentence, and fixes the safe things with a single click. And if you sell online, it protects your store too: orders, checkout and payments.

Free features:

  • Security scan with a 0–100 score — 13 real checks (outdated WordPress, users exposed through the REST API, XML-RPC left on, author enumeration, public readme.html, missing security headers, debug mode, default database prefix, SSL, PHP version, an account named “admin”, automatic updates) each with a plain-language explanation.
  • Deep file scan — every file examined one by one, on demand and weekly: core files against the official WordPress checksums, plugins and themes file-by-file against a baseline photo, executable files hiding in uploads, and high-risk code patterns reported as suspicions, never verdicts — plus a structural heuristic layer that scores the SHAPE of the code (long encoded strings, decode-and-execute chains, visitor input turned into code, chopped-up obfuscation) with plain-language reasons, so machine-generated malware is flagged even when no known signature matches. The heuristic only reports: it never quarantines or touches a file by itself. It runs in chunks for shared hosting, and it deletes nothing — it only reports, down to the exact file. The results live in their own Scan view, cleaned up: no duplicate rows, the standard “Silence is golden” guard files are never flagged, warnings inside bundled libraries (phpseclib, Guzzle, Google API…) are grouped into one expandable row per library instead of hundreds of loose lines, and the headline separates real criticals, new or changed files and library groups. On paid plans, Bruno’s AI adds a “What you should do” verdict under the results, from the grouped summary only.
  • Owner signature (passkey) — sign in with your fingerprint, face or PIN instead of a code: the private key is sealed inside your device’s secure chip, so it cannot be phished, copied or leaked from a database. And the crown-jewel actions — creating or promoting an administrator, changing the site email, installing or activating plugins, turning this plugin off, saving payment-gateway settings — demand a fresh signature, so a stolen password and session are no longer enough.
  • Mini firewall that explains itself — and blocks on paid plans — every request is quietly checked against generic attack patterns (SQL injection, cross-site scripting, file-inclusion and traversal tricks, remote-file parameters, and probes of sensitive files like wp-config, .env or backup archives). Everything it sees is written down in plain words in the new Activity view (“Someone tried to read the server’s internal files — High risk — It did not get in”), with the raw technical line one click away. On the free plan it only watches. On paid plans it also BLOCKS clear attacks with a 403 — safely: a 7-day learning mode first (it marks what it WOULD have blocked and cuts nothing), a local decision made by the plugin’s own patterns (no server orders these blocks), an emergency watch-only switch, and two hard rules: your allowlist is never blocked and a signed-in administrator is never blocked.
  • Sensor Network (optional, off until you say yes) — if you opt in, your site becomes a sensor of the Vidal Security network: it shares ATTACK data only (the attacker’s IP, what was tried, the pattern family matched, the path without parameters, and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the sample) so an IP that attacks one site gets flagged for all. It NEVER shares your content, your users, your customers or request bodies — and nothing is sent until an administrator accepts the notice shown in wp-admin. The switch lives in the plugin panel and can be turned off anytime.
  • One-click hardening, fully reversible — hide the user list from the REST API for visitors, disable XML-RPC, block author enumeration, hide the WordPress version, add security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS on HTTPS), and block readme.html / license.txt.
  • A dashboard with its own identity — your score front and center, color-coded status cards, and clear next steps. No cryptic logs.

🛒 WooCommerce protection (free, included):

Running a store? Then the money side matters as much as the site itself. These guards switch on automatically when WooCommerce is active — and only then:

  • Order anti-fraud — every order receives a local risk score (IP velocity, disposable email addresses, billing/shipping country mismatch, high-value first orders, failed-payment bursts), a traffic-light badge in the orders list, a downloadable evidence file for chargeback disputes, and an email alert when the risk is high.
  • Checkout guard — an invisible anti-bot honeypot plus a minimum fill time on the classic checkout form, and a payment-attempt limiter that stops card testing (3 failed payments in 1 hour = a 30-minute checkout block). The limiter and the IP blocks cover both the classic checkout and the block checkout (Store API); the honeypot, the minimum fill time and the optional Turnstile apply to the classic form, because the block checkout does not send those form fields.
  • Payments & webhook monitor — an hourly watch for WooCommerce webhooks silently disabled, paid orders stuck without moving, and waves of failed payments, with clear email alerts that distinguish an attack from a gateway failure.

Optional AI Guardian (premium service):

With a site key, the plugin can connect to the Vidal Security AI cloud service (operated by Vidal Digital Miami on n8n) to classify attacks with AI, receive temporary IP blocks ordered by the service, and show a daily “guard’s report” in plain language. This connection is optional and off by default. Your dashboard shows the agent as the Sentinel: a live card with your agent on watch — events watched, IPs blocked, last and next round — and the daily watch rounds log, written in plain language every morning. On the free version, the same card shows the agent asleep, and exactly what you are missing while it sleeps.

Privacy: Your data is yours. We do not sell your data, we do not use it for advertising, and we never train anything with it. Without a site key, the plugin sends nothing about your site anywhere – every free feature runs inside your own site (including loopback requests to your own homepage, used only when you press “Scan now”). Two transparent exceptions: copies obtained directly from Vidal Digital Miami check our own server for plugin updates, like any self-hosted plugin (see “External services”); and, ONLY if an administrator opts in to the Sensor Network, the plugin sends attack data (attacker IP, event type, pattern family, path without parameters, SHA-256 sample fingerprint, plus your site’s host and WordPress/plugin/PHP versions) to the Vidal Security service so attacking IPs can be flagged network-wide. No personal data of yours or your visitors is included, reports are kept 90 days, and opting out stops all sharing immediately.

External services

This plugin can optionally connect to the Vidal Security AI cloud service, operated by Vidal Digital Miami, to power the premium AI Guardian. The connection is off by default and only happens when the site owner explicitly enables the AI Guardian and enters a site key in the plugin’s settings.

  • What is sent, and when: when the AI Guardian is enabled, the plugin sends technical security events in batches (about once an hour) to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/webhook/sec-ingest. Each event contains only: event type, IP address, user agent, requested path, and attempted username for login-related events. It also reads this site’s own report from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/webhook/sec-report. No site content, no customer data, no order data and no passwords are ever sent.
  • Why: the service classifies the events with AI (noise vs. real threat), can order temporary IP blocks back to the plugin, and produces the daily plain-language guard’s report. Urgent alerts by WhatsApp, when enabled for the site, are sent by the service.
  • Terms of service: https://vidaldigitalmiami.com/vidal-security-ai-terms.html
  • Privacy policy: https://vidaldigitalmiami.com/vidal-security-ai-privacy.html

Free-license counter (off until you activate it): the plugin offers an optional, free license. Nothing is sent anywhere until an administrator clicks “Activate FREE license” in the plugin’s admin notice. That click sends exactly three things to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/contador — the plugin’s name, this site’s URL and the plugin version — so Vidal can count active installations. While the license is active, a weekly heartbeat repeats those same three data points (and learns whether the license is Free or Pro). If you delete the plugin, it notifies the same service so the copy stops counting. No emails, no users, no content — and the plugin works fully whether you activate the license or not.

Vulnerability definitions (automatic download — nothing about your site is sent): the known-vulnerability check runs on a definitions database that this plugin downloads from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/downloads/ (first the small bruno-vuln-manifest.json, then the database file it names). The download happens automatically about every 12 hours, the file’s checksum is verified before it is adopted, and the check itself runs entirely on your site. It is a plain download of a public file: the request sends no site data, no inventory and no personal information.

Sensor Network (only with your explicit consent): the dashboard asks whether you want to share attack data with the Vidal Security network. Nothing is sent before you agree, and you can switch it off at any time. With consent on, the plugin sends attack reports to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/red-sensores: attacker IP, event type, pattern family, the path tried (without parameters) and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the sample — never emails, usernames, content or request bodies.

Network intelligence feed (Guardian key, or Sensor consent): sites with an active AI Guardian — or that opted into the Sensor Network — periodically download a signed IP-reputation package from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/red-inteligencia, identifying themselves with their site key or sensor ID. The package signature is verified before anything is applied. Sites that never enable either feature never contact this endpoint.

WordPress.org checksum service: during a deep file scan, core files are compared against the official checksums served by https://api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/ — WordPress.org’s own service, sending only your WordPress version and locale.

Cloudflare Turnstile (only if you configure it): the checkout guard can use Cloudflare Turnstile, only when you enter your own Turnstile keys in the plugin settings; the browser then loads https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js and verifications go to Cloudflare. With no keys configured, nothing is loaded or sent.

Updates: this copy contains no updater of its own — it updates through WordPress.org like any other plugin in this directory. (Copies downloaded directly from Vidal Digital Miami include their own update channel; that mechanism is not present here.)
sections.installation:
1. Upload the vidal-security-ai folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Vidal Security in the admin menu and press Scan now.
  4. Turn on the hardening switches you want and press Save. Everything is reversible.
sections.faq:
Does the free version phone home?

It never sends your site’s data anywhere. The only HTTP requests it triggers are loopback requests to your own site (only when you run a manual scan) and, in copies obtained directly from Vidal Digital Miami, a version check against our update server (v8.vidalbooking.com/downloads) so WordPress can offer you plugin updates – no site data is included in that check.

One opt-in exception, spelled out in plain words: the FREE license. Activating it is free, needs no card and is optional. When an administrator activates it, the site sends Vidal’s center only three data points — the site URL, the plugin name and its version — nothing else: no emails, no users, no content. Its only job is counting active installations; a weekly heartbeat keeps the count current and, if the plugin is ever uninstalled, the center is notified and the copy stops counting. The plugin works in full whether you activate it or not, and if the center does not answer, your site does not even notice.

Will the hardening break my site?

Each switch is conservative and reversible. The only file ever touched is .htaccess, only for the readme/license block, only on Apache/LiteSpeed servers where the file is writable, and the rules are written between clearly marked # BEGIN Vidal Security AI / # END Vidal Security AI markers. Turning the switch off (or deactivating the plugin) removes them.

What does the AI Guardian add?

AI classification of attacks (noise vs. real threat), smart temporary IP blocks, a shared threat reputation network, and a daily plain-language report. It requires a site key and is a paid subscription service; the free plugin remains fully functional without it.

Does it work on multisite?

It is designed and tested for single-site installs in this version.
sections.changelog:
1.29.7

  • FIXED (EN): Bruno’s deep-scan verdict can now actually reach your panel. The verdict collection asked for the Guardian’s report through a helper that did not exist and looked for the verdict in the wrong place inside the report, so the verdict stayed “waiting” forever even when the service had already answered. The collection now reads the verdict from the Guardian report exactly where the service puts it, and the “What you should do” block shows Bruno’s verdict — with its evidence — as soon as it arrives. No other behaviour changes.
  • ARREGLADO (ES): el veredicto de Bruno sobre el escaneo profundo ya puede llegar a tu panel. La recogida del veredicto pedía el reporte del Guardián a través de una función que no existía y buscaba el veredicto en el lugar equivocado dentro del reporte, así que el veredicto se quedaba «en espera» para siempre aunque el servicio ya hubiera respondido. La recogida ahora lee el veredicto del reporte del Guardián exactamente donde el servicio lo pone, y el bloque «Qué debes hacer» muestra el veredicto de Bruno — con su evidencia — en cuanto llega. Ningún otro comportamiento cambia.

1.29.6

  • FIX (EN): this release aligns the WordPress.org build with what this directory requires. The direct-channel updater is NOT included in this copy (copies from WordPress.org update through WordPress.org), and every remaining connection is now declared under “External services” with its exact trigger: the free-license counter contacts Vidal’s center only after an administrator clicks “Activate FREE license” (before that click, nothing is sent), the Sensor Network only after your explicit consent, the intelligence feed only with an AI Guardian key or that same consent, and the vulnerability-definitions download — automatic, verified by checksum — sends nothing about your site. No security feature changes: same scanner, same hardening, same Guardian.
  • CORRECCIÓN (ES): esta versión alinea la build de WordPress.org con lo que este directorio exige. El actualizador del canal directo NO va incluido en esta copia (las copias de WordPress.org se actualizan desde WordPress.org), y cada conexión restante queda declarada en «External services» con su disparador exacto: el contador de licencias FREE solo contacta con la central de Vidal después de que un administrador pulse «Activar licencia FREE» (antes de ese clic no se envía nada), la Red de Sensores solo tras tu consentimiento expreso, el paquete de inteligencia solo con una clave del Guardián IA o ese mismo consentimiento, y la descarga de definiciones de vulnerabilidades — automática, verificada por suma de control — no envía nada de tu sitio. Ninguna función de seguridad cambia: el mismo escáner, el mismo endurecimiento, el mismo Guardián.

1.29.5

  • NEW (EN): the vulnerability check now runs on Bruno’s own vulnerability database — the “antivirus” model. The database is built centrally every 6 hours from free public sources (the NVD and CISA’s KEV catalogue of vulnerabilities known to be exploited), published with a definitions version, and this plugin downloads it automatically (on activation and every 12 hours), verifies its checksum before adopting it, and crosses your PHP, WordPress, plugins and theme against it LOCALLY on your own site. No AI is used for detection on any plan, nothing about your site is sent anywhere for this check, and if a download ever fails the previous database keeps protecting you. The panel shows the definitions version your site carries (“Vulnerability database: version … · updated … · N rules · M known exploited (KEV)”), and findings that CISA confirms are being actively exploited are flagged as such. The database is a gift on every plan, Free included — and because the local check and Bruno’s cloud check now read the SAME database, the two can no longer disagree. The previous per-component queries to the WP Vulnerability API are retired.
  • NUEVO (ES): la revisión de vulnerabilidades ahora funciona con la base de datos propia de Bruno — el modelo «antivirus». La base se construye en la central cada 6 horas desde fuentes públicas y gratuitas (la NVD y el catálogo KEV de CISA de vulnerabilidades explotadas conocidas), se publica con su versión de definiciones, y este plugin la descarga automáticamente (al activar y cada 12 horas), verifica su suma de control antes de adoptarla y cruza tu PHP, WordPress, plugins y tema contra ella EN LOCAL, en tu propio sitio. La detección no usa IA en ningún plan, no se envía nada de tu sitio a ningún sitio para esta revisión, y si una descarga falla alguna vez, la base anterior te sigue protegiendo. El panel muestra la versión de definiciones que lleva tu sitio («Base de vulnerabilidades: versión … · actualizada … · N reglas · M explotadas conocidas (KEV)»), y los hallazgos que CISA confirma en explotación activa quedan marcados como tales. La base es un regalo en todos los planes, el Free incluido — y como la revisión local y la del Guardián en la nube ahora leen LA MISMA base, ya no pueden discrepar. Se retiran las consultas por componente a la API de WP Vulnerability.

1.29.4

  • FIXED (EN): the vulnerability check no longer blames a site for vulnerabilities that belong to a DIFFERENT edition or line of a product. Some products keep parallel lines (for example a Free 3.x line and a Pro 7.x line): if the database lists a flaw “fixed in 7.6.4” for the Pro line, a site running the latest Free 3.x is not vulnerable — Bruno now files those cases separately as “Not counted — different product line”, shows them for transparency, and never counts them as vulnerabilities of your site. Findings whose declared affected range starts inside your installed line are still reported exactly as before.
  • NEW (EN): the deep file scan adds a structural heuristic layer. On top of the known risk patterns, every PHP file now gets a structural score — long encoded strings hidden in the code, decode-and-execute chains (eval of base64/gzinflate), visitor input turned into code, code chopped into hundreds of hand-joined pieces — each finding with its score and its reasons in plain words. This catches machine-generated, shape-shifting malware that has no known signature. It only reports: nothing is quarantined or deleted automatically, and the threshold is adjustable (option/filter).
  • ARREGLADO (ES): la revisión de vulnerabilidades ya no culpa a un sitio por vulnerabilidades que pertenecen a OTRA edición o línea del producto. Algunos productos mantienen líneas paralelas (por ejemplo una línea Free 3.x y una Pro 7.x): si la base lista un fallo «corregido en 7.6.4» de la línea Pro, un sitio con la última Free 3.x no es vulnerable — Bruno ahora aparta esos casos como «No contado — línea distinta del producto», los muestra por transparencia y nunca los cuenta como vulnerabilidades de tu sitio. Los hallazgos cuyo rango afectado declarado arranca dentro de tu línea instalada se siguen reportando exactamente igual que antes.
  • NUEVO (ES): el escaneo profundo de archivos añade una capa de heurística estructural. Además de los patrones de riesgo conocidos, cada archivo PHP recibe ahora una puntuación por su FORMA — cadenas codificadas largas escondidas en el código, cadenas de decodificar-y-ejecutar (eval de base64/gzinflate), datos del visitante convertidos en código, código partido en cientos de trozos unidos a mano — cada hallazgo con su puntuación y sus motivos en lenguaje simple. Así se caza también el malware generado por máquina que cambia de forma y no tiene firma conocida. Solo reporta: nada se pone en cuarentena ni se borra solo, y el umbral es ajustable (opción/filtro).

1.29.2

  • IMPROVED (EN): the deep file scan now shows a live progress bar while it runs — real data from the scan itself (files found while listing, then files examined out of the total with its percentage), refreshed without reloading the page. And Bruno’s verdict moves to the TOP of the Scan view, right under the scan summary and before the findings list, so what you should do is the first thing you read after a scan.
  • IMPROVED (EN): the vulnerability check is reordered the same way: the “Check now” button now sits at the top of the Vulnerabilities view with its own live progress bar (components checked out of the total, and the component being checked), and the results stay underneath.
  • MEJORA (ES): el escaneo profundo de archivos ahora muestra una barra de progreso viva mientras corre — datos reales del propio escaneo (archivos encontrados durante el listado y, después, archivos examinados sobre el total con su porcentaje), refrescada sin recargar la página. Y el veredicto de Bruno pasa ARRIBA de la vista Escaneo, justo bajo el resumen del escaneo y antes de la lista de hallazgos, para que lo que debes hacer sea lo primero que leas tras un escaneo.
  • MEJORA (ES): la revisión de vulnerabilidades se reordena igual: el botón «Revisar ahora» queda arriba de la vista Vulnerabilidades, con su propia barra de progreso viva (componentes revisados sobre el total, y el componente en curso), y los resultados quedan debajo.

1.29.1

  • NEW (EN): a “Go Pro” button at the top of the panel, shown whenever the site is not on a paid plan yet — free licence or no licence at all — linking straight to the purchase page in a new tab. It hides itself once a paid plan (PRO licence or active AI Guardian) is on.
  • NUEVO (ES): botón «Hazte Pro» arriba del panel, visible siempre que el sitio no tenga un plan de pago — licencia FREE o sin licencia — con enlace directo a la página de compra en pestaña nueva. Se oculta solo cuando hay un plan de pago activo (licencia PRO o Guardián IA activo).

1.29.0

  • NEW (EN): the panel is reorganized into Panel · Activity · Scan · Vulnerabilities. The firewall log moves to Activity and speaks plainly: every attempt says what they tried (“Someone tried to read the server’s internal files”, “Someone looked for a forgotten backup file”), the risk in words (High/Medium/Low) and how it ended (“It did not get in” / “Blocked”), with the raw technical line under a “Technical detail” toggle. The deep file scan gets its own Scan view, cleaned up: no duplicate rows, the standard “Silence is golden” guard index.php is no longer flagged (a real executable in uploads still is), and warnings inside bundled libraries are grouped into one expandable row per library and component — the headline now separates real criticals, new or changed files and library groups instead of one giant “to review” number. The vulnerability check moves to its own Vulnerabilities view; the dashboard shows only its summary.
  • NEW (EN): paid plans — the mini firewall now BLOCKS clear attacks (SQL injection, XSS, file inclusion, sensitive-file probes) with a 403, decided locally by the plugin’s own patterns. Safety net: a mandatory 7-day learning mode first (it records what it WOULD have blocked and cuts nothing), an emergency watch-only switch in Activity, and two hard rules — your allowlist is never blocked and a signed-in administrator is never blocked. Free keeps watching, exactly as before.
  • NEW (EN): paid plans — Bruno’s verdict under the scan: the AI Guardian receives the GROUPED summary of each scan (never the thousands of raw rows, at most one request per scan, cached with the scan) and answers with a “What you should do” block in plain words: what is normal and can be marked as known, what needs a look, and what is fixed by updating which component.
  • NUEVO (ES): el panel se reorganiza en Panel · Actividad · Escaneo · Vulnerabilidades. El registro del firewall pasa a Actividad y habla claro: cada intento dice qué intentaron («Alguien intentó leer los archivos internos del servidor», «Alguien buscó una copia de seguridad olvidada»), el riesgo en palabras (alto/medio/bajo) y cómo terminó («No lo consiguió» / «Bloqueado»), con la línea técnica cruda bajo un desplegable «Detalle técnico». El escaneo profundo de archivos gana su vista propia, Escaneo, y viene limpio: sin filas duplicadas, el index.php guardián estándar («Silence is golden») ya no se marca (un ejecutable de verdad en uploads sí), y los avisos dentro de librerías empaquetadas se agrupan en una fila expandible por librería y componente: el titular separa críticos reales, archivos nuevos o cambiados y grupos de librerías, en vez de una cifra gigante «por revisar». La revisión de vulnerabilidades pasa a su vista propia, Vulnerabilidades; el panel principal solo muestra su resumen.
  • NUEVO (ES): planes de pago — el mini firewall ahora BLOQUEA los ataques claros (inyección SQL, XSS, inclusión de archivos, sondeo de archivos sensibles) con un 403, decidido en local por los patrones del propio plugin. Red de seguridad: primero 7 días obligatorios en modo aprendizaje (anota lo que HABRÍA bloqueado y no corta nada), interruptor de emergencia «solo mirar» en Actividad, y dos reglas duras: tu lista blanca nunca se bloquea y un administrador conectado tampoco. El plan gratis sigue vigilando, igual que siempre.
  • NUEVO (ES): planes de pago — el veredicto de Bruno bajo el escaneo: el Guardián IA recibe el resumen AGRUPADO de cada escaneo (nunca los miles de filas crudas, como máximo una petición por escaneo, guardada junto al escaneo) y responde con el bloque «Qué debes hacer» en palabras claras: qué es normal y puede marcarse como conocido, qué hay que revisar y qué se arregla actualizando qué componente.

1.28.0

  • NEW (EN): vulnerability check on every site where the plugin is installed. Bruno compares the installed versions of WordPress, your plugins and your theme against the public WP Vulnerability database and shows, in plain language, which components have known vulnerabilities, how serious each one is and which version fixes it. The check button is available to everyone, Free included; paid plans (PRO licence or AI Guardian) also get an automatic daily check and an email to the administrator when a new critical or high vulnerability appears. It is a data cross-check — no AI cost — and results are cached for 12 hours. Honest scope: published vulnerabilities with a detectable version only; it is not a penetration test.
  • NUEVO (ES): revisión de vulnerabilidades en cada sitio donde el plugin esté instalado. Bruno compara las versiones instaladas de WordPress, tus plugins y tu tema contra la base pública WP Vulnerability y muestra, en lenguaje claro, qué componentes tienen vulnerabilidades conocidas, qué tan grave es cada una y qué versión la corrige. El botón de revisión está disponible para todos, Free incluido; los planes de pago (licencia PRO o Guardián IA) tienen además revisión automática diaria y un correo al administrador cuando aparece una vulnerabilidad crítica o alta nueva. Es un cruce de datos — sin coste de IA — y los resultados se guardan en caché 12 horas. Alcance honesto: solo vulnerabilidades publicadas con versión detectable; no es un pentest.

1.27.6

  • CHANGED (EN): the Guardian’s brain (n8n / Vidal Flow) is no longer a switch in the settings panel. It is assigned by Vidal for your site key — before, flipping it out of curiosity disconnected the Guardian, because only the brain tied to your key answers. The panel now simply shows which brain your site uses. Existing sites keep exactly the brain they already had, and a brain only changes when Vidal assigns it from the server. No changes to the site’s protection.
  • CAMBIADO (ES): el cerebro del Guardián (n8n / Vidal Flow) ya no es un interruptor en el panel de ajustes. Lo asigna Vidal según tu clave de sitio: antes, cambiarlo por curiosidad desconectaba el Guardián, porque solo responde el cerebro asociado a tu clave. Ahora el panel solo muestra qué cerebro usa tu sitio. Los sitios existentes conservan exactamente el cerebro que ya tenían, y un cerebro solo cambia cuando Vidal lo asigna desde el servidor. Sin cambios en la protección del sitio.

1.27.5

  • FIXED (EN): the shared Vidal licence module is updated to the canonical copy. Activating the FREE licence can no longer be blocked by another Vidal plugin on the same site — before, when a sibling plugin’s activation handler ran first, the click died with “The link you followed has expired” and the licence never activated. The module also learns the licence plan (FREE/PRO) from the center on activation and keeps it current on the weekly heartbeat. No changes to the site’s protection.
  • CORREGIDO (ES): el módulo compartido de licencias de Vidal se actualiza a la copia canónica. Activar la licencia FREE ya no puede quedar bloqueado por otro plugin Vidal en el mismo sitio: antes, cuando el gestor de activación de un plugin hermano corría primero, el clic moría con «El enlace que has seguido ha caducado» y la licencia nunca se activaba. El módulo además aprende el plan de la licencia (FREE/PRO) desde la central al activarla y lo mantiene al día en el latido semanal. Sin cambios en la protección del sitio.

1.27.4

  • NEW (EN): Bruno has a new face. The Sentinel is no longer a cartoon guard: he is a real veteran — an experienced security professional keeping watch over your site, shown in the dashboard as the AI guardian he is. Same watch, same rounds; now with a face that has years behind it.
  • NUEVO (ES): Bruno tiene cara nueva. El Centinela ya no es un guardia de dibujos: es un veterano de verdad — un profesional de seguridad con experiencia vigilando tu sitio, mostrado en el panel como el guardián IA que es. La misma vigilancia, las mismas rondas; ahora con una cara con años detrás.

1.27.2

  • FIXED (EN): sites with the Guardian active no longer see the FREE licence invitation and are not counted as free installations — a premium site’s identity is its site key. If a site once activated the FREE licence and later turns the Guardian on, its free count simply fades after 45 days without a heartbeat.
  • CORREGIDO (ES): los sitios con el Guardián activo ya no ven la invitación a la licencia FREE ni cuentan como instalación gratuita: la identidad de un sitio premium es su clave de sitio. Si un sitio activó antes la FREE y después enciende el Guardián, su conteo gratuito decae solo a los 45 días sin latido.

1.27.1

  • CLARIFIED (EN): the admin notice and this readme now spell out, in plain words, what the FREE license does — what data travels (site URL, plugin name and version, nothing else), the weekly heartbeat, the notice on uninstall, that the plugin works fully without it, and that an unreachable center changes nothing on your site. No functional changes.
  • ACLARADO (ES): el aviso del administrador y este readme ahora explican con todas las letras qué hace la licencia FREE — qué datos viajan (la URL del sitio, el nombre del plugin y su versión, nada más), el latido semanal, el aviso al desinstalar, que el plugin funciona completo sin ella y que si la central no responde no cambia nada en tu sitio. Sin cambios funcionales.

1.27.0

  • NEW (EN): FREE license activation — direct copies can now activate a free license from the admin notice: one click registers the installation in Vidal’s official install counter (only the site URL and the plugin version travel), a weekly heartbeat keeps the count honest, and uninstalling notifies the center so the copy stops counting. The plugin works fully with or without the license, and if the center is unreachable nothing changes on your site.
  • NUEVO (ES): activación de licencia FREE — las copias directas ya pueden activar una licencia gratuita desde el aviso del administrador: un clic registra la instalación en el contador oficial de Vidal (solo viajan la URL del sitio y la versión del plugin), un latido semanal mantiene el conteo honesto y, al desinstalar, el plugin avisa a la central para dejar de contar. El plugin funciona completo con o sin licencia, y si la central no responde no cambia nada en tu sitio.

1.26.2

  • FIX (EN): version label alignment — the 1.26.1 package bumped the internal version constant but not the plugin header line, so the Plugins list kept showing 1.26.0 while the 1.26.1 code was running. No functional changes.
  • CORRECCIÓN (ES): alineada la etiqueta de versión — el paquete 1.26.1 subió la constante interna de versión pero no la línea de cabecera del plugin, así que la lista de Plugins seguía mostrando 1.26.0 mientras corría el código 1.26.1. Sin cambios funcionales.

1.26.1

  • FIX (EN): The deep file scan no longer wanders into neighboring websites. On shared hosting, the account’s other domains live as folders inside this site’s root — the first live scan swept 320,465 files across the whole account and flagged the neighbor’s own WordPress core files as critical. Any folder with its own wp-config.php + wp-admin/ is another site and is now skipped entirely: not entered, not counted, not judged, and its files in an old baseline no longer report as “deleted”. The report notes how many neighboring sites were skipped.
  • CORRECCIÓN (ES): El escaneo profundo ya no se mete en los sitios vecinos. En el hosting compartido, los demás dominios de la cuenta viven como carpetas dentro de la raíz de este sitio: el primer escaneo en vivo barrió 320.465 archivos de toda la cuenta y marcó como críticos los archivos del núcleo del vecino. Toda carpeta con su propio wp-config.php + wp-admin/ es otro sitio y ahora se salta entera: no se entra, no se cuenta, no se juzga, y sus archivos en una foto vieja ya no salen como «borrados». El informe anota cuántos sitios vecinos se saltaron.

1.26.0

  • NEW — Owner signature (passkey): the sign-in that cannot be stolen. Register a passkey from your profile — fingerprint, face or PIN, with user verification always required — and the private key stays sealed in your device’s secure chip: the site keeps only the public half, so phishing cannot copy it and a leaked database gives an attacker nothing usable. At sign-in, the signature REPLACES the two-factor code for anyone who has one (with the code kept as a fallback on the same screen). The crown-jewel actions demand a FRESH signature, valid 10 minutes and tied to your session: creating or promoting an administrator, changing the site email, installing or activating plugins, deactivating this plugin, and saving WooCommerce payment-gateway settings. A site policy can require every administrator to register one. The site admin is emailed on every registration and revocation, and another administrator can revoke a lost device from the user’s profile, exactly like two-factor rescue. Honest limits: signatures are bound to your site’s domain (change the domain and they must be registered again); ES256 and RS256 keys only.
  • REBUILT — Deep file scan engine: after its first live run wedged at 0 files on a real 41,510-file store, the engine was rewritten end to end. The panel card now works with buttons and AJAX — no redirect chains and no forms nested inside the profile form — the file queue and the new baseline photo live in protected files under uploads (denied to the web) instead of one giant database option, and even the tree listing advances in chunks. A scan state left wedged by the old engine heals itself instead of hanging forever, and the weekly cron scan runs the same engine. Detection is unchanged: official core checksums, per-file baseline diff, executables in uploads, risk patterns as suspicions.
  • ES: NUEVO — Firma del dueño (passkey): el acceso que no se puede robar. Registra una llave desde tu perfil — huella, cara o PIN, con verificación de usuario siempre obligatoria — y la llave privada queda sellada en el chip seguro de tu dispositivo: el sitio guarda solo la mitad pública, así que el phishing no puede copiarla y una base de datos filtrada no le da al atacante nada usable. Al entrar, la firma SUSTITUYE al código de dos factores para quien la tenga (el código queda como respaldo en la misma pantalla). Las acciones corona exigen una firma FRESCA, válida 10 minutos y atada a tu sesión: crear o ascender un administrador, cambiar el correo del sitio, instalar o activar plugins, desactivar este plugin y guardar los ajustes de las pasarelas de pago de WooCommerce. Una política del sitio puede exigir que todo administrador registre la suya. El administrador del sitio recibe un correo en cada registro y cada revocación, y otro administrador puede revocar un dispositivo perdido desde el perfil del usuario, igual que el rescate de dos factores. Límites honestos: las firmas van atadas al dominio del sitio (si el dominio cambia, hay que registrarlas de nuevo); solo llaves ES256 y RS256.
  • ES: REHECHO — Motor del escaneo profundo de archivos: tras atascarse en 0 archivos en su primera corrida real sobre una tienda de 41.510 archivos, el motor se reescribió entero. La tarjeta del panel ahora funciona con botones y AJAX — sin cadenas de redirecciones ni formularios anidados —, la cola de archivos y la foto base nueva viven en archivos protegidos dentro de uploads (denegados a la web) en vez de en una opción gigante de la base de datos, y hasta el listado del árbol avanza por trozos. Un estado atascado heredado del motor viejo se autocura en vez de colgar para siempre, y el escaneo semanal por cron usa el mismo motor. La detección no cambia: sumas oficiales del núcleo, diferencias por archivo contra la foto, ejecutables en uploads y patrones de riesgo como sospechas.

1.25.1

  • FIX — Deep file scan: the step chain now advances through self-posting pages (the nonce travels in the POST body) instead of expiring redirect links — on its first live run (Fresh Flowers, 41,510 files) the old chain died at the first step with “The link you followed has expired” and left the scan marked as running. The panel card also gains “Continue scan” and “Stop and reset” controls while a scan is in progress, so an interrupted scan is never wedged again.
  • ES: CORRECCIÓN — Escaneo profundo: la cadena de pasos ahora avanza con páginas que se autoenvían por POST (el nonce viaja en el cuerpo) en vez de enlaces de redirección que caducan — en su primera corrida en vivo (Fresh Flowers, 41.510 archivos) la cadena vieja murió en el primer paso con «The link you followed has expired» y dejó el escaneo marcado en curso. La tarjeta del panel gana además los botones «Continuar escaneo» y «Detener y reiniciar» mientras haya un escaneo en marcha, para que un escaneo interrumpido no quede atascado nunca.

1.25.0

  • NEW — Deep file scan: every file, one by one, on demand and weekly. Core files (wp-admin, wp-includes) are compared against the OFFICIAL WordPress checksums for your version — modified is critical, unknown or missing is flagged; if the checksum service is unreachable, the core falls back to the local baseline and the panel says so. Plugins, themes, mu-plugins and loose PHP are compared file-by-file against a baseline photo (the exact file that changed, appeared or vanished — the daily change watch only knew the folder). Executable files found inside uploads are critical. PHP code in wp-content is also checked for high-risk patterns (eval, gzinflate, commands fed from visitor input, very long base64, remote includes, known shell markers) — reported as a SUSPICION, never as confirmed malware. The scan runs in chunks so it survives shared-hosting time limits, deletes and changes NOTHING, emails the admin when it finds critical items, and any exact file can be marked “known” so it is not flagged again unless it changes. Pattern checks skip vendor folders.
  • ES: NUEVO — Escaneo profundo de archivos: cada archivo, uno por uno, a petición y cada semana. Los archivos del núcleo (wp-admin, wp-includes) se comparan con las sumas OFICIALES de WordPress para tu versión — modificado es crítico; desconocido o ausente queda señalado; si el servicio de sumas no responde, el núcleo cae a la línea base local y el panel lo dice. Plugins, temas, mu-plugins y PHP suelto se comparan archivo a archivo contra una foto base (el archivo exacto que cambió, apareció o desapareció — la vigilancia diaria solo conocía la carpeta). Un ejecutable dentro de uploads es crítico. El código PHP de wp-content pasa además por patrones de alto riesgo (eval, gzinflate, comandos alimentados desde la entrada del visitante, base64 muy largo, includes remotos, marcadores de shells conocidas) — reportado como SOSPECHA, jamás como malware confirmado. El escaneo corre por trozos para sobrevivir a los límites de tiempo del hosting compartido, no borra ni cambia NADA, avisa por correo si encuentra críticos, y cualquier archivo exacto puede marcarse «conocido» para no volver a señalarlo salvo que cambie. Los patrones saltan las carpetas vendor.

1.24.0

  • NEW — Country Guard: block visits from the countries you choose, right at the door. The country comes only from Cloudflare’s CF-IPCountry header — a site that is not behind Cloudflare sees no country and the module stays inert instead of guessing. Off by default and switched on per site in its own panel card, with the country list validated against ISO codes. Logged-in administrators, allowlisted IPs and verified good bots are never blocked, and blocks are counted per country and day without storing visitor IPs. Nothing about these blocks is reported to the network.
  • ES: NUEVO — Bloqueo por país: cierra la puerta a las visitas de los países que elijas. El país se lee solo de la cabecera CF-IPCountry de Cloudflare — un sitio que no esté detrás de Cloudflare no ve país y el módulo queda inerte en vez de adivinar. Apagado por defecto y encendido por sitio en su propia tarjeta del panel, con la lista validada contra los códigos ISO. Nunca …

short_description: Security for WordPress and WooCommerce: plain-language scan, one-click hardening, order anti-fraud, checkout guard and payment monitoring.
description:
Most security plugins speak in logs and codes. Vidal Security AI speaks like a person: it scans your site, gives you a clear 0–100 score, explains every problem in one plain sentence, and fixes the safe things with a single click. And if you sell online, it protects your store too: orders, checkout and payments.

Free features:

  • Security scan with a 0–100 score — 13 real checks (outdated WordPress, users exposed through the REST API, XML-RPC left on, author enumeration, public readme.html, missing security headers, debug mode, default database prefix, SSL, PHP version, an account named “admin”, automatic updates) each with a plain-language explanation.
  • Deep file scan — every file examined one by one, on demand and weekly: core files against the official WordPress checksums, plugins and themes file-by-file against a baseline photo, executable files hiding in uploads, and high-risk code patterns reported as suspicions, never verdicts — plus a structural heuristic layer that scores the SHAPE of the code (long encoded strings, decode-and-execute chains, visitor input turned into code, chopped-up obfuscation) with plain-language reasons, so machine-generated malware is flagged even when no known signature matches. The heuristic only reports: it never quarantines or touches a file by itself. It runs in chunks for shared hosting, and it deletes nothing — it only reports, down to the exact file. The results live in their own Scan view, cleaned up: no duplicate rows, the standard “Silence is golden” guard files are never flagged, warnings inside bundled libraries (phpseclib, Guzzle, Google API…) are grouped into one expandable row per library instead of hundreds of loose lines, and the headline separates real criticals, new or changed files and library groups. On paid plans, Bruno’s AI adds a “What you should do” verdict under the results, from the grouped summary only.
  • Owner signature (passkey) — sign in with your fingerprint, face or PIN instead of a code: the private key is sealed inside your device’s secure chip, so it cannot be phished, copied or leaked from a database. And the crown-jewel actions — creating or promoting an administrator, changing the site email, installing or activating plugins, turning this plugin off, saving payment-gateway settings — demand a fresh signature, so a stolen password and session are no longer enough.
  • Mini firewall that explains itself — and blocks on paid plans — every request is quietly checked against generic attack patterns (SQL injection, cross-site scripting, file-inclusion and traversal tricks, remote-file parameters, and probes of sensitive files like wp-config, .env or backup archives). Everything it sees is written down in plain words in the new Activity view (“Someone tried to read the server’s internal files — High risk — It did not get in”), with the raw technical line one click away. On the free plan it only watches. On paid plans it also BLOCKS clear attacks with a 403 — safely: a 7-day learning mode first (it marks what it WOULD have blocked and cuts nothing), a local decision made by the plugin’s own patterns (no server orders these blocks), an emergency watch-only switch, and two hard rules: your allowlist is never blocked and a signed-in administrator is never blocked.
  • Sensor Network (optional, off until you say yes) — if you opt in, your site becomes a sensor of the Vidal Security network: it shares ATTACK data only (the attacker’s IP, what was tried, the pattern family matched, the path without parameters, and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the sample) so an IP that attacks one site gets flagged for all. It NEVER shares your content, your users, your customers or request bodies — and nothing is sent until an administrator accepts the notice shown in wp-admin. The switch lives in the plugin panel and can be turned off anytime.
  • One-click hardening, fully reversible — hide the user list from the REST API for visitors, disable XML-RPC, block author enumeration, hide the WordPress version, add security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS on HTTPS), and block readme.html / license.txt.
  • A dashboard with its own identity — your score front and center, color-coded status cards, and clear next steps. No cryptic logs.

🛒 WooCommerce protection (free, included):

Running a store? Then the money side matters as much as the site itself. These guards switch on automatically when WooCommerce is active — and only then:

  • Order anti-fraud — every order receives a local risk score (IP velocity, disposable email addresses, billing/shipping country mismatch, high-value first orders, failed-payment bursts), a traffic-light badge in the orders list, a downloadable evidence file for chargeback disputes, and an email alert when the risk is high.
  • Checkout guard — an invisible anti-bot honeypot plus a minimum fill time on the classic checkout form, and a payment-attempt limiter that stops card testing (3 failed payments in 1 hour = a 30-minute checkout block). The limiter and the IP blocks cover both the classic checkout and the block checkout (Store API); the honeypot, the minimum fill time and the optional Turnstile apply to the classic form, because the block checkout does not send those form fields.
  • Payments & webhook monitor — an hourly watch for WooCommerce webhooks silently disabled, paid orders stuck without moving, and waves of failed payments, with clear email alerts that distinguish an attack from a gateway failure.

Optional AI Guardian (premium service):

With a site key, the plugin can connect to the Vidal Security AI cloud service (operated by Vidal Digital Miami on n8n) to classify attacks with AI, receive temporary IP blocks ordered by the service, and show a daily “guard’s report” in plain language. This connection is optional and off by default. Your dashboard shows the agent as the Sentinel: a live card with your agent on watch — events watched, IPs blocked, last and next round — and the daily watch rounds log, written in plain language every morning. On the free version, the same card shows the agent asleep, and exactly what you are missing while it sleeps.

Privacy: Your data is yours. We do not sell your data, we do not use it for advertising, and we never train anything with it. Without a site key, the plugin sends nothing about your site anywhere – every free feature runs inside your own site (including loopback requests to your own homepage, used only when you press “Scan now”). Two transparent exceptions: copies obtained directly from Vidal Digital Miami check our own server for plugin updates, like any self-hosted plugin (see “External services”); and, ONLY if an administrator opts in to the Sensor Network, the plugin sends attack data (attacker IP, event type, pattern family, path without parameters, SHA-256 sample fingerprint, plus your site’s host and WordPress/plugin/PHP versions) to the Vidal Security service so attacking IPs can be flagged network-wide. No personal data of yours or your visitors is included, reports are kept 90 days, and opting out stops all sharing immediately.

External services

This plugin can optionally connect to the Vidal Security AI cloud service, operated by Vidal Digital Miami, to power the premium AI Guardian. The connection is off by default and only happens when the site owner explicitly enables the AI Guardian and enters a site key in the plugin’s settings.

  • What is sent, and when: when the AI Guardian is enabled, the plugin sends technical security events in batches (about once an hour) to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/webhook/sec-ingest. Each event contains only: event type, IP address, user agent, requested path, and attempted username for login-related events. It also reads this site’s own report from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/webhook/sec-report. No site content, no customer data, no order data and no passwords are ever sent.
  • Why: the service classifies the events with AI (noise vs. real threat), can order temporary IP blocks back to the plugin, and produces the daily plain-language guard’s report. Urgent alerts by WhatsApp, when enabled for the site, are sent by the service.
  • Terms of service: https://vidaldigitalmiami.com/vidal-security-ai-terms.html
  • Privacy policy: https://vidaldigitalmiami.com/vidal-security-ai-privacy.html

Free-license counter (off until you activate it): the plugin offers an optional, free license. Nothing is sent anywhere until an administrator clicks “Activate FREE license” in the plugin’s admin notice. That click sends exactly three things to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/contador — the plugin’s name, this site’s URL and the plugin version — so Vidal can count active installations. While the license is active, a weekly heartbeat repeats those same three data points (and learns whether the license is Free or Pro). If you delete the plugin, it notifies the same service so the copy stops counting. No emails, no users, no content — and the plugin works fully whether you activate the license or not.

Vulnerability definitions (automatic download — nothing about your site is sent): the known-vulnerability check runs on a definitions database that this plugin downloads from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/downloads/ (first the small bruno-vuln-manifest.json, then the database file it names). The download happens automatically about every 12 hours, the file’s checksum is verified before it is adopted, and the check itself runs entirely on your site. It is a plain download of a public file: the request sends no site data, no inventory and no personal information.

Sensor Network (only with your explicit consent): the dashboard asks whether you want to share attack data with the Vidal Security network. Nothing is sent before you agree, and you can switch it off at any time. With consent on, the plugin sends attack reports to https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/red-sensores: attacker IP, event type, pattern family, the path tried (without parameters) and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the sample — never emails, usernames, content or request bodies.

Network intelligence feed (Guardian key, or Sensor consent): sites with an active AI Guardian — or that opted into the Sensor Network — periodically download a signed IP-reputation package from https://v8.vidalbooking.com/flow/red-inteligencia, identifying themselves with their site key or sensor ID. The package signature is verified before anything is applied. Sites that never enable either feature never contact this endpoint.

WordPress.org checksum service: during a deep file scan, core files are compared against the official checksums served by https://api.wordpress.org/core/checksums/1.0/ — WordPress.org’s own service, sending only your WordPress version and locale.

Cloudflare Turnstile (only if you configure it): the checkout guard can use Cloudflare Turnstile, only when you enter your own Turnstile keys in the plugin settings; the browser then loads https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js and verifications go to Cloudflare. With no keys configured, nothing is loaded or sent.

Updates: this copy contains no updater of its own — it updates through WordPress.org like any other plugin in this directory. (Copies downloaded directly from Vidal Digital Miami include their own update channel; that mechanism is not present here.)
